newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway urges EU sanctions against Iran.
newsitem.headline: Norway urges EU sanctions against Iran.

text.p: Norway, which severed relations with Tehran almost two years ago, called on the European Union on Friday to consider imposing trade sanctions on Iran, a Foreign Ministry official said.
He said Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal made the call in a meeting with EU ambassadors in Oslo.

Godal earlier said he hoped for an international economic boycott of Iran following a German court ruling on Thursday accusing Iran's leaders of having sanctioned the murders of a group of Iranian Kurdish leaders in a Berlin restaurant in 1992.

"This ruling is incredibly important because it is the first time we have got a final verdict from a western court stating clearly that Iranian authorities are acting in violation of international law," Godal told Norwegian television.
Norway, the world's second biggest oil exporter, is not a member of the European Union.
Norway's volume of trade with Iran has been minimal since Oslo withdrew its ambassador from Tehran and downgraded trade relations in July 1995.
This was in protest against Iran's refusal to denounce the edict passed by late Iranian spiritual leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini in 1989 against British novelist Salman Rushdie.

Relations between Oslo and Tehran deteriorated after William Nygaard, head of the Oslo publishing house that brought out Rushdie's "The Satanic Verses" in Norwegian, was shot and wounded outside his Oslo home in October 1993. Iran has denied any involvment in the attack and no suspects have been arrested.
